_comment: Multi-GPU (tensor-parallel) benchmark config, written for a 4-GPU Linux box (validated on 4x NVIDIA A40 48 GB). TensorSharp vs llama.cpp on the same GGUFs, across text / multi-turn / tool / structured / image / audio / video scenarios, at --tp 1, 2 and 4. Select it with: python run_matrix.py --config benchmark_config_multigpu.json --tp 1,2,4 (report.py takes the same --config). TENSOR PARALLELISM: defaults.tp_devices lists the GPU ids the harness may use; every launched server is pinned to the first N of them (CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES), so a --tp N cell really occupies N GPUs and the tp=1 baseline really occupies one. TensorSharp splits with `--tp N`, llama.cpp with `--split-mode tensor`. A model too big for one GPU declares `min_tp` (DeepSeek V4 Flash UD-Q8_K_XL is ~154 GB, so it only runs at tp=4 on this box) and its smaller-degree cells are recorded as skipped instead of OOMing. MODEL PROVISIONING: every model declares its Hugging Face `source`, so any missing file is downloaded into ${model_root} on the first run and reused afterwards (`--download never` to require local files, `--download force` to re-fetch); files whose remote name differs from the local one carry their own `url`. Retarget with BENCH_MODEL_ROOT / BENCH_LLAMA_SERVER / BENCH_TS_SERVER_DLL / BENCH_RESULTS / BENCH_TP_DEVICES / BENCH_IMAGE / BENCH_AUDIO / BENCH_VIDEO.

gemma4-e4b._max_tp_note: the attention KV-head count (2) must be divisible by the TP degree, so TensorSharp accepts --tp 1 or 2 only

gemma4-26b-a4b._mmproj_note: the published GGUF mmproj for this model is vision-only (clip.has_audio_encoder is absent), unlike E4B's — so no audio scenario here
gemma4-26b-a4b._max_tp_note: 2 KV heads: TensorSharp rejects --tp 4 at load time (Gemma4 TP validation: KV heads must be divisible by the TP degree)

qwen35-35b-a3b._max_tp_note: the attention KV-head count (2) must be divisible by the TP degree, so TensorSharp accepts --tp 1 or 2 only

nemotron3-omni-30b.display: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Nano Omni 30B-A3B Reasoning (UD-IQ4_XS, MoE omni)
nemotron3-omni-30b._mmproj_note: despite the Omni name, the published GGUF mmproj carries only the vision tower (nemotron_v2_vl projector, no audio encoder)
nemotron3-omni-30b._max_tp_note: the attention KV-head count (2) must be divisible by the TP degree, so TensorSharp accepts --tp 1 or 2 only

dsv4-flash._tp_note: DeepSeek V4 has its own whole-model executor and passes tpDegree=1 to ModelBase, so --tp N here is NOT the ggml tensor-parallel path (no AllReduce): N is reinterpreted as the number of GPUs its executor LAYER-splits the 150.7 GiB of weights across. That is what makes the model hostable at all; it is capacity parallelism, not a throughput axis, so read its tp4 row as the only configuration that runs rather than as a scaling point.

text_short.description: Short single-turn text prompt (~2k-token context preamble)

text_long.description: Long-context single-turn text prompt (~2k-token context preamble + passage)

multi_turn.description: 3-turn conversation (~2k-token context preamble), timed on the final turn

json_mode.description: Structured output (response_format json_object) with ~2k-token context preamble

backends._comment: ggml_cuda is the apples-to-apples column (both engines on the same ggml CUDA kernels). `cuda` is TensorSharp's own direct-CUDA backend — no llama.cpp equivalent, so that column is TensorSharp-only. Both declare CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES as the device-pinning variable used by the --tp axis (it is also the inferred default for cuda-tagged backends). llama.cpp tensor parallelism uses --split-mode tensor (weights + KV, NCCL-backed); --split-mode row is gone from current CUDA builds. NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1 is set for llama.cpp because this host ADVERTISES peer access between all four A40s but does not honour it: with P2P left on, llama-server spins forever in its first NCCL collective (95% CPU, never becomes ready) instead of loading. TensorSharp probes for this at startup and falls back on its own, so it needs no such flag.
